articles.title: À peine lancée cet été, Google Maps perd l’une de ses meilleures fonctionnalités sur Android Auto
articles.text:
À peine lancée cet été, Google Maps perd l’une de ses meilleures fonctionnalités sur Android Auto
Plusieurs utilisateurs de Google Maps sur Android Auto sont confrontés à un bug assez contraignant depuis quelques jours : le compteur de vitesse et les limitations ont subitement disparu de leur écran.
Déployé depuis quelques semaines sur Android Auto, le compteur de vitesse en temps réel de Google Maps venait enfin combler une lacune historique face à Apple CarPlay. Une avancée de courte durée, puisque de nombreux automobilistes déplorent déjà la disparition soudaine de cette fonction, accompagnée de celle des limitations de vitesse. Ce retour en arrière, inattendu après des années d’attente, s'apparente heureusement à un bug d’affichage temporaire plutôt qu’à un retrait définitif.
Bug Android Auto : le compteur et les limitations de vitesse s'effacent de Google Maps
Longtemps réservé à l’app mobile et disponible sur Apple CarPlay depuis l’été 2024, le compteur de vitesse en direct avait enfin fait son entrée sur Android Auto au cours du mois de juillet. Associé aux limitations de vitesse, cet ajout très réclamé par la communauté offrait ainsi tout l’essentiel pour garder un œil sur son allure au volant. Mais alors que son déploiement à grande échelle venait d'être amorcé, la situation s’est brutalement inversée.
Des dysfonctionnements sont en effet de plus en plus signalés sur Reddit, ces indicateurs ayant déserté l’interface du jour au lendemain. Du côté de CarPlay, rien n’a bougé et l'affichage demeure fonctionnel. Le problème ne s’arrête d’ailleurs pas là, puisque certains conducteurs rapportent également la disparition simultanée des feux tricolores, des panneaux stop et des lignes de trafic.
	
Aujourd’hui, j’ai remarqué que le compteur et les limitations ont disparu. C’est également le cas pour les panneaux stop et les feux.
Disparition des limitations sur Maps : quelle solution temporaire ?
Pour l’heure, aucune solution universelle n’a été publiée, que ce soit du côté de la communauté Reddit ou de Google. Plusieurs utilisateurs expliquent toutefois avoir retrouvé la fonction en quittant les canaux bêta de Google Maps et d’Android Auto pour réinstaller des versions stables de l'app. Une astuce qui ne fonctionne malheureusement pas à tous les coups.
Alors que Waze subit lui aussi quelques ratés d’affichage, Google n’a pas encore réagi officiellement. En attendant le déploiement d’un correctif via une prochaine mise à jour, les automobilistes doivent donc se résoudre à surveiller leur compteur physique et la signalisation routière.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max launch with a familiar design, new A20 Pro SoC, and aperture-controlled camera
articles.text:
Through the looking glass: A new camera with the first-ever aperture controls on an iPhone is the main star of this year's iPhone presentation. With the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple is introducing a more versatile camera, more powerful photo-customization software, and yet another tech giant's attempt to distinguish authentic images from AI-generated creations.
Pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max open on September 12, with availability beginning September 18 starting at $1,199. As previously rumored, Apple seems to have delayed the standard iPhone 18 until next year.
The iPhone 18 Pro is the first iPhone to support aperture control. With six blades and a new sensor, users can smoothly switch between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 apertures to control lighting and depth of field, as well as enhance low-light photography.
Users can also apply new texture styles and cinematic effects to videos recorded at up to 60fps. Additionally, time-lapse mode now supports 4K and Dolby Vision HDR recording. Meanwhile, the new iPhone adjusts the Dynamic Island to show up to three Live Activities simultaneously while still enabling Face ID.
Like Google and other developers, Apple also aims to provide a tool for watermarking AI-edited photos and verifying unaltered images. Apple Reference Image creates a duplicate of each new photo with cloud-processed, signed sensor data to prevent editing. Users can compare it with the copy they normally use to check for changes. A new API also makes reference images available to third-party apps, but the feature's resilience against ever-evolving AI tools in the wild remains untested.
The processor in this year's iPhone also receives another die shrink. The A20 Pro features TSMC's new 2-nanometer process, increasing memory bandwidth by 50% and GPU performance by 40% over the iPhone 17 Pro's A19 Pro. A new dual 16-core Neural Engine also enhances photography and AI performance, powering the iPhone 18's new photo features and iOS 27's AI-powered Siri.
A new vapor chamber improves thermal performance by 40%, while a new battery design extends the iPhone 18 Pro's maximum battery life to 36 hours and the iPhone 18 Pro Max's to 45 hours. The standard model can charge to 50% in approximately 15 minutes via a wired connection or 30 minutes wirelessly.
Storage options include 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and a new 2TB tier. Available colors include burgundy, glacier, silver, and black.

articles.title: Apple debuts $129 AirPods 5 with better noise cancellation and transparency mode
articles.text:
Apple has debuted the new AirPods 5 with improved active noise cancellation and sound quality—aiming to provide improved listening and user features at a lower launch price than the predecessor AirPods 4.
The newest AirPods will go on sale for $129 in stores starting on September 18, according to an Apple press release accompanying the company’s “Surprise and Shine” event. Customers can also purchase AirPods 5 with a wireless charging case that provides longer battery life and on-stem volume control for $149. Preorders are already open.
This is looking like a solid deal compared to the predecessor AirPods 4. The older AirPods debuted in 2024 with a starting price of $129, but users had to pay $179 for the version with active noise cancellation.
The new AirPods 5 come with active noise cancellation that supposedly removes up to 50 percent more noise in comparison with the AirPods 4—an improvement that Apple credits to a new multiport acoustic architecture and better computational audio algorithms.
Improved transparency mode for the AirPods 5 also allows users to more naturally hear nearby sounds in their immediate vicinity, like people’s voices.
The device’s adaptive audio automatically shifts between active noise cancellation and transparency mode depending on the background noise, said Dave Pakula, VP of hardware engineering for Apple, during the Apple presentation.

articles.title: Apple's first foldable is called iPhone Duo. It costs $2,999
articles.text:
Apple finally unveiled its first foldable iPhone, called the iPhone Duo.
In the reveal, Apple showed off several design elements to achieve the foldable, including a hidden, under-display selfie camera on the inner display, and having both displays use the same aspect ratio to ensure a seamless experience.
The iPhone Duo also leverages some of the innovation from last year’s iPhone Air, like pushing hardware into the camera bump to make the rest of the device thinner.
Elsewhere, Apple pushed several software changes to iOS to adapt to both the foldable capabilities and the larger inner display. UI elements like the dock and status bar have moved to the side of the device, ensuring they’re both easily accessible. iOS now supports opening multiple apps side-by-side.
iPhone Duo will also work with Apple Pencil later this year.
Touch ID also makes a comeback as the main way to unlock the iPhone Duo, along with support for unlocking via Apple Watch.
All-new software approach
Later in the keynote, Apple offered a more in-depth look at the UI changes. For multitasking, there are several new gestures for using two apps at the same time, like the ability to pair apps together so they open side-by-side.
The company also showed off the ability to use Duo while partially folded, with iOS automatically moving things away from the middle of the display so they’re easier to reach.
Apple updated several other iPhone features to take advantage of the folding display, such as new StandBy modes.
Hardware that’s all about the details
The iPhone Duo sports a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display. The inner screen sports a premium, nano-texture finish to reduce glare and reflections while also minimizing crease visibility. Apple also detailed its efforts to improve durability, including using grade five titanium for the frame and Ceramic Shield 2 on the front display for better scratch resistance.
Apple also detailed the tech behind the inner display and hinge. The display sports a scratch-resistance coating and nano-texture cover layer that’s 40 per cent stiffer than other materials used in the industry. Glass sits above and below the folding display panel, and the display uses a custom adhesive to allow the various layers to slide over each other, which reduces stress when bending.
Powered by A20 Pro, the iPhone Duo offers plenty of power to handle everything you want to do. The foldable also boasts all-day battery life, with Apple putting batteries on both sides of the device. A rebalancing algorithm allows both cells to operate seamlessly together for up to 31 hours of video playback using the inner display, or 44 with the outer display.
The foldable also sports fast charging, able to get up to a 50 per cent charge in about 20 minutes with a wire, or 30 minutes wirelessly.
The iPhone Duo sports two rear cameras, including a 48MP primary sensor and a 12MP 2x telephoto camera. The main camera is the same as the main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro.
FaceTime also gets some upgrades, leveraging all the cameras, enabling users to show both what’s in front of and behind the phone.
Elsewhere, Apple showed off smart camera features, like the Duo’s ability to automatically snap shots when everyone is posed, meaning one person doesn’t need to be left out of the shot anymore.
Availability in Canada
iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order starting October 16 and will release on October 23. It will only support eSIM, and will start at $2,999.
Along with the iPhone Duo, Apple is launching new accessories to go along with the foldable. For example, there’s a new folio case with an integrated kickstand, while the new Duo Case has a protective two-part design.

articles.title: OpenAI says its next-generation processors could be made at Samsung — double-sourcing with TSMC hints at massive volume requirements
articles.text:
OpenAI says its next-generation processors could be made at Samsung — double-sourcing with TSMC hints at massive volume requirements
Samsung may join TSMC producing OpenAI's next-generation AI ASICs.
OpenAI is expanding its relationship with Samsung beyond memory supply and enterprise software as the AI giant plans to outsource production of at least some of its processors to Samsung Foundry, Harrison Kim, General Manager of OpenAI Korea, revealed this week. If the information is accurate, then OpenAI will source its AI accelerators from both TSMC and Samsung Foundry, which suggests massive volume requirements.
"One of the areas where we have made the most progress and gained the most recognition with Samsung Electronics is our joint production and research on the next-generation chips we are developing," said Harrison Kim, General Manager of OpenAI Korea, at a press conference in Seoul, Reuters reports.
OpenAI already has its own AI ASIC program that relies on Broadcom's design services as well as TSMC's wafer processing and advanced packaging services. So far, the company has introduced its first inference AI accelerator called Jalapeño that was defined by the company's engineers, then co-designed with Broadcom, then made by TSMC, all in less than 18 months.
OpenAI did not explain whether Samsung's participation concerns a second production source for Jalapeño, another processor under development by OpenAI, a chip jointly developed by Samsung and OpenAI, or some other aspect of chip production and development. Samsung and SK hynix already supply memory for OpenAI's Stargate data center initiative, though joint chip development and production barely have a relation to DRAM supply.
OpenAI's 1st Generation Jalapeño will unlikely be double-sourced from TSMC and Samsung because the chip is already in mass production at TSMC and OpenAI is talking about 'next-generation chips,' not the ones that are in mass production at the moment. Furthermore, development of Jalapeño's successor is well underway and is approaching tapeout, which means that its mass production is not far away either. Since OpenAI's claim clearly involves 'next-generation chips,' it is entirely possible that OpenAI will indeed produce its 2nd Generation inference ASIC at Samsung Foundry.
Back in late July, Samsung Electronics and Broadcom announced a strategic partnership valued at over $200 billion through 2030 to collaborate on advanced foundry, memory, and packaging technologies for AI infrastructure. Hence, as OpenAI has an agreement with Broadcom to procure 10GW of custom AI accelerators, it will be able to produce these accelerators at both Samsung and TSMC. Of course, if it needs silicon produced at Samsung, and pays Broadcom for appropriate design porting.
Perhaps, OpenAI will take a page from Tesla's book and will double-source Jalapeño's successor from TSMC and Samsung to get higher volumes. However, Tesla's volume requirements may be different from those of OpenAI.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Tesla needs extraordinary AI5 volumes because it intends to use the processor across three very different high-volume applications: AI data centers, vehicles, and Optimus robots. Therefore, Tesla could potentially need millions of AI5 chips for cars alone, on top of robots and data-center deployments. Therefore, paying for separate TSMC and Samsung physical implementations gives Tesla not only supply-chain resilience but also aggregate capacity necessary to supply several product categories.
Yet, data center accelerators tend to be vastly more silicon-intensive per unit compared to ASICs for vehicles or robots. If OpenAI/Broadcom's next ASIC is a large leading-edge processor with multiple dies and OpenAI wants gigawatts of these processors, wafer requirements could still become too high for TSMC alone (which is fully booked by the likes of AMD and Nvidia). In that situation, OpenAI may need another foundry to get enough ASICs. Still, we are speculating.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Can't see your speed or traffic data on Google Maps in Android Auto? You're not alone — here's what we know about the issues
articles.text:
The Google Maps speedometer has started disappearing on Android Auto — and some users are also missing traffic data
Here's what's happening
- Some Android Auto users are missing the Google Maps speedometer
- The feature only recently rolled out to a wider group of people
- Real-time traffic data on the map has also vanished for a number of users
Google Maps has only recently started showing speed limit information on Android Auto screens — so recently that it hasn't reached everyone yet — but now users are reporting that the speedometer has started disappearing unexpectedly, together with real-time traffic data in some cases.
Reports appearing on Reddit (via 9to5Google) suggest the problem isn't affecting everyone, and comes and goes intermittently, but is definitely a real issue. Stop signs and traffic signals also appear to be affected by the same bug.
Some commenters on Reddit are saying that the speedometer shows up in Android Auto when connected to the phones of some family members but not others. That might indicate the problem is related to a specific Android or app version somehow.
Other users say the bug is connected to switching to or from the beta versions of Android Auto and Google Maps, which could be another explanation of what's happening. For now though, Google hasn't officially acknowledged that there's an issue.
Affecting some but not all
The problem of real-time traffic information not showing up has actually been going on for longer, and seems to be sticking around. Again, it doesn't look like a vast number of users are affected, but the bug is definitely having an impact for some.
With so many different Android device models, software versions (including betas), and vehicle types involved, it's perhaps no surprise that annoyances like this crop up from time to time — but that doesn't make the experience any less frustrating for users.
At least one Redditor in the main complaints thread has already quit Google Maps over the decision to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America in the app, under the direction of the White House, which does mean no need to worry any more about these bugs.

The good news for everyone who's sticking around is that Google regularly rolls out updates for Android, Google Maps, and Android Auto, and so we're hoping that these problems are sorted sooner rather than later. In the meantime, if you're seeing these issues, you'll just have to sit tight and wait for a fix to appear.

articles.title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Massachusetts became the latest state to force data centers to bring their own power, but this time there’s a twist. A new state mandate would require developers building data centers larger than 25 megawatts to provide clean power or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.
Gov. Maura Healey’s executive order is the latest example of states turning against data centers. Just a few years ago, tech companies and data center developers were showered with incentives to locate facilities in a particular state. Now, they’re fighting a groundswell of public opposition as politicians seek to show voters they’re addressing their concerns.
Under Healey’s order, data centers larger than 25 megawatts of peak demand will have to bring their own power and guarantee that it adheres to the state’s clean energy requirements. Healey would prefer that they generate the clean power onsite, too. If not, they’ll need to fund the construction of new generation nearby or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.
Massachusetts is also directing communities to “avoid signing non-disclosure agreements,” according to the executive order. To give regulators time to implement the new restrictions, the governor is pausing applications for a data center sales tax exemption that went into effect last month.
The clean power commitment might not be as stringent as it sounds, though. Healey said data centers must meet the Massachusetts clean energy standard enshrined in state law, which means they will only have to generate a portion of their power using approved sources like wind, solar, and hydro. In 2030, for example, those sources must contribute at least 40% of the total. The amount varies by year, and it ratchets up over time.
TechCrunch was unable to reach Healey’s office prior to publication.
With the new restrictions, Massachusetts becomes the third state in as many months to rein in data center development.
In August, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott announced that all new data centers in the state would need to submit to audits by the public utility commission and the grid operator, ERCOT. In July, New York’s governor stopped construction of new data centers 50 megawatts or larger.
With public sentiment shifting against data centers, the tech industry is starting to push back. Pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future — which is funded by Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and Greg Brockman — is buying ads that seek to sway voters in battleground states ahead of midterm elections.

articles.title: 'What's left for the 26H2 update then?': not much frankly — Windows 11's latest update packs the 3 key changes that most folks are waiting for
articles.text:
Windows 11's September update has arrived — here are the 3 key features that make this a must-install upgrade
Start, taskbar and Windows 11 search goodness
- Windows 11's latest update has arrived
- The September update brings in the ability to move the taskbar
- There are also new options for resizing the Start menu, and a really useful tweak for Windows 11's search function
Windows 11's latest update has arrived, and it packs some important new features for the interface of the desktop OS.
Bleeping Computer flagged all the additions in the September 2026 update for Windows 11, and there are three major highlights, which I'll pick out here, before providing a general roundup of some of the other tweaks that Microsoft has brought in this month.
As ever, some of these features are being rolled out in a phased manner, so even if you do install the September update today, you may still have to wait a while for certain pieces of functionality to make their way over to your PC.
1. A movable taskbar
Thanks to the September update you'll finally be able to move Windows 11's taskbar away from the bottom of the screen, to the top instead, or the sides if you prefer (an option that people with an ultra-wide monitor often want to use, as it suits that aspect ratio much better).
This is an ability which has always been in Windows 10, but was dropped for Windows 11 because porting it over was a thornier issue than you might think (or so Microsoft told us).
Finally, however, Microsoft has got its act together and the taskbar can now be repositioned in Windows 11 – although I've a feeling this will be one of the features on a slower rollout. Hopefully I'll be wrong on that score and you'll get this ability promptly if you've been keenly awaiting it for the last five years.
It's also worth noting that there's another option introduced here which can make the taskbar smaller, so it takes up less screen real-estate on devices with small displays.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
2. The Start menu can now be resized
Want a more compact Start menu? Your wish is Microsoft's command, as this choice has now been introduced to the Settings app for the Start menu. You can elect to have a standard (large) menu, or a small one, rather than leaving it at the default 'automatic' setting whereby Windows 11 chooses the size itself based on your device. The problem with leaving the OS to decide is that sometimes you get the bigger menu on a laptop screen, where it pretty much eats the whole desktop – and so in these scenarios you can now manually choose the more compact Start menu.
With options to remove sections of the Start menu coming on top of this, you can now trim this part of the interface down so it's truly minimal. This choice will be more important than the movable taskbar for many folks – myself included – and it's great to see it now being rolled out.
3. Windows 11 search improvements
Another notable boon with the September update is that there are a few changes for Windows 11's core search functionality, and the most important is a new option that lets you turn off web results in search.
When you're searching for a file on your local drive, those web results often get in the way, so it'll be a relief for many to be able to switch them off. As well as web results (which open in Edge, with searches in Bing, of course), you can also turn off Microsoft Store suggestions. Essentially this is a general decluttering of Windows 11 search which is long overdue, frankly.
Other features in Windows 11's September Update
There's a performance boost for File Explorer in that the Home page now loads faster, and switching between virtual desktops in Windows 11 is now snappier, too.
Microsoft has made some reliability tweaks as well, including ensuring that the app history information in Task Manager is correct, and also that interacting with the Display panel within Settings is now more stable.
Furthermore, Microsoft informs us that there are some design tweaks here: "This update introduces updated progress indicators across Windows, providing a more consistent and modern experience during startup, sign-in, restart, shutdown, and update installation."
It's also worth noting that the weird mouse bug that affected the preview version of this September update (the optional update released at the end of August) has been resolved.
There's a fair bit happening here, and as one Redditor put it: "What's left for the 26H2 [update] then?"
Well, not a great deal in truth, and if you've been following along with Microsoft's annual updates, you may recall that 26H2 is going to be a very minor upgrade that doesn't do a lot. Indeed, some folks are wondering why Microsoft didn't save these juicy new interface features for 26H2, given that it's out next month.
The reason is likely to be because Microsoft wants to ensure that 26H2 runs as smoothly as possible (with no bigger changes involved). Although to be fair, as noted, due to the rollout process, a lot of folks won't be getting the new Start menu options and taskbar repositioning until October (or possibly later) anyway.

articles.title: LEDs Push Wireless Power Further - EE Times
articles.text:
Japanese researchers have developed an indoor, LED-based wireless power system that uses adaptive optics and AI-guided beam control to power IoT devices up to 5 meters away, both day and night. The optical wireless power transmission (OWPT) system maintains a tightly focused LED beam for longer-distance energy transfer while precisely directing that light to multiple photovoltaic receivers, even during changing light conditions that can interrupt optical tracking and reduce power delivery.
Lead researcher Professor Tomoyuki Miyamoto from the Institute of Science Tokyo highlighted how LEDs offer a safer option for indoor wireless power transfer than the more widely developed laser-based systems. “The lower radiance and power density of LEDs make it easier to design systems that comply with optical safety requirements,” he told EE Times. “LEDs are also relatively cheap, have long operating lifetimes, and can be integrated into lighting-like modules.”
Miyamoto is also confident that his OWPT system will play a key role in safe and sustainable IoT infrastructure in buildings: “This is a stable and versatile wireless power transmission solution. Its most likely initial applications are indoor sensor networks in factories, farms, and smart buildings, where the delivered power can remain modest.”
Beyond RF limits
RF power transfer is already used in distributed IoT applications, including low-power sensor systems in buildings and warehouses, reducing reliance on batteries and wired connections. However, the technology faces issues around efficiency, range, and electromagnetic interference. For example, free-space propagation losses reduce the power available at the receiver as distance increases, while stray EMI emissions can disrupt connectivity.
In recent years, laser-based OWPT has emerged for longer-distance wireless power delivery, with systems demonstrating transmission over tens of meters. By concentrating energy into a narrow optical beam, laser approaches can achieve higher power densities than RF systems while avoiding RF interference concerns. However, safety considerations remain a major barrier for indoor deployment, creating interest in LED-based OWPT.
Miyamoto and his team unveiled their first LED-based approach back in 2019, which used collimating and focusing optics to efficiently transmit optical power across 1 meter. But as Miyamoto pointed out, longer transmissions suffered severe power attenuation as the LED beam diverged, reducing optical power density at the receiver, while the system also struggled to operate reliably under varying lighting conditions. The latest AI-guided adaptive optics system addresses these limitations.
In a bid to overcome power attenuation problems and extend transmission distances beyond a meter, the researchers used an adaptive double-layer lens, comprising a liquid lens with a tunable focal length and a fixed imaging lens. These more sophisticated beam-shaping optics were designed using ray-tracing simulations to balance key parameters such as LED beam collection, the actual beam spot size, and transmission distance.
“By dynamically adjusting the liquid-lens focal length to suppress [LED] beam expansion … effective power transmission up to 5 meters has been demonstrated,” Miyamoto said. “Also, the optical power received at 3 meters was around 8× higher than the previous fixed-optics system.” Miyamoto also pointed out how simulations indicated that the LED beam could remain focused for up to 10 meters, although he and colleagues haven’t yet demonstrated this in their experiments.
To direct the tightly focused LED beam toward photovoltaic receivers, the system uses a motorized reflector that is adjusted according to data captured by an RGB-IR depth camera. The camera identifies the receivers and determines where the beam should be directed based on their size and location. On-board AI, using a convolutional neural network based on a single-shot object-detection algorithm, further hones detection accuracy.
To ensure operation in darkness, retroreflective sheets—commonly used on traffic signs and safety clothing—are attached to the edges of the PV receivers to reflect light from the depth camera’s IR sensor and create a clear outline of each receiver. “The reflected pattern is captured with high contrast, allowing the system to locate a PV receiver even when the room lighting is switched off,” Miyamoto said.
Five-meter demo
Experimental tests look good. Miyamoto and his team placed five different-sized PV receivers, 2 to 4 meters apart, around their lab, powering each one sequentially. Their LED-based OWPT system was able to locate and seamlessly switch between each receiver in both light and dark conditions, efficiently transmitting power up to 5 meters.
“Under illuminated conditions, medium and large receivers were detected at up to 5 meters, while under unlit conditions, retroreflector-equipped receivers were reliably detected at approximately 4 meters,” Miyamoto said.
However, as he also noted: “Our LED system is primarily intended for meter-scale indoor applications. For transmissions over tens of meters or when high power is needed, a laser-based system becomes more practical.”
Further improvements are also possible. According to Miyamoto, the overall optical system efficiency came in at just over 56%, but the researchers now intend to raise this to more than 80%. Possible routes forward include using a more focused LED or mounting a microlens onto the LED to reduce the spread of light and get more light into the system’s beam-shaping optics. The researchers also hope to characterize the relationship between the temperature of the liquid lens and its focal length so they can introduce thermal compensation to prevent the focal drift that reduces receiver tracking precision.
“As well as lens-system efficiency, our next steps are to increase recognition robustness, integrate the optical source and power electronics, and evaluate long-term reliability,” Miyamoto said. “If we can now get an industry partner to look at product integration and qualification, we will be able to build a pilot system relatively quickly.”

articles.title: Apple dévoile les iPhone 18 Pro, deux nouveaux monstres de puissance et d'endurance
articles.text:
Lors de la keynote, Apple a dévoilé une nouvelle génération d’iPhone haut de gamme, composée de deux modèles, l’iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. Selon la marque, c’est évidemment « le meilleur iPhone Pro jamais conçu ». Contrairement aux années précédentes, Apple n’accompagne pas ses deux téléphones premium d’une édition standard plus abordable. Aucun iPhone 18 standard n’a été présenté lors de la keynote. Par contre, Apple a dévoilé l’iPhone Duo, son tout premier iPhone avec un écran pliant.
À lire aussi : AirPods 5 – voici les deux nouveaux modèles d’écouteurs sans fil d’Apple
Un design qui évolue… un peu
Sur le plan du design, Apple a opté pour une évolution plutôt qu’une révolution. Le châssis reprend globalement celui de l’iPhone 17 Pro, avec le même bloc photo proéminent à l’arrière. En fait, le changement visuel le plus visible se situe en haut de l’écran. La Dynamic Island, l’îlot qui dissimule les capteurs de reconnaissance faciale, a rétréci, laissant plus de place pour l’affichage. Côté coloris, Apple mise sur du noir, de l’argent, du bleu glacier, et du bordeaux. Sans surprise, le bordeaux est la grande couleur de l’année.
L’iPhone 18 Pro est recouvert d’un écran OLED de 6,3 pouces, avec taux de rafraîchissement adaptatif ProMotion jusqu’à 120 Hz. Plus imposant, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max hérite d’un écran de 6,9 pouces. Pas de surprise de ce côté-là !
Un appareil photo jamais vu chez Apple
La grande nouveauté de l’iPhone 18 Pro se trouve côté photo. L’iPhone 18 Pro inaugure l’ouverture variable sur son objectif principal. C’est une première chez Apple. Un système mécanique ajuste désormais l’ouverture du diaphragme pour mieux maîtriser la profondeur de champ. Six petites lamelles en composite, taillées au laser, s’ouvrent ou se referment devant le capteur comme le ferait l’iris d’un œil. Le triple module reste composé d’un capteur principal, d’un téléobjectif et d’un ultra grand-angle, tous en 48 mégapixels.
Pour Greg Joswiak, le responsable du marketing d’Apple, ce nouvel appareil photo « permet à tous de prendre facilement des photos et des vidéos exceptionnelles grâce à l’ouverture variable, tout en offrant une plus grande polyvalence aux créateurs et un contrôle accru aux professionnels ». Comme toujours, Apple présente son iPhone Pro comme le smartphone idéal pour les créateurs, les photographes et les vidéastes. Les professionnels bénéficient particulièrement de l’ouverture variable, puisqu’ils peuvent ajuster manuellement les quatre paliers d’ouverture directement depuis l’application Appareil photo, détaille Apple.
La puissance de la puce A20 Pro
Sous le capot, la nouvelle puce A20 Pro est gravée en 2 nanomètres par TSMC. Là encore, c’est une première pour Apple. C’est la même finesse de gravure que celle utilisée pour la puce Apple M6. Le géant de Cupertino annonce un gain de performances plutôt conséquent. La nouvelle puce Apple A20 Pro embarque un GPU à sept cœurs, promettant jusqu’à 40% de gains de performances comparé à l’A19 Pro. Côté processeur, l’A20 Pro compte six cœurs CPU au total : deux “super cœurs” haute performance et quatre cœurs plus économes en énergie. Apple affirme que ces deux gros cœurs sont, de loin, les plus rapides de toute l’industrie du semi-conducteur. La bande passante mémoire de l’A20 Pro progresse de 50%.
Le moteur neuronal de l’A20 Pro a lui aussi été revu, avec l’ajout de deux modules supplémentaires, portant le total à 32 cœurs. Cette évolution permet de doubler les performances dédiées à l’intelligence artificielle. C’est évidemment l’idéal pour faire tourner Apple Intelligence, la suite d’outils IA du groupe, au cœur de la keynote, ainsi que le nouveau Siri AI, également au centre de la conférence. Comme prévu, Apple a amélioré le système de refroidissement. Ce système améliore considérablement les performances de l’iPhone en dissipant mieux la chaleur. L’écran a également été repensé pour bénéficier d’un refroidissement plus efficace.
L’autonomie en forte hausse
Apple en profite aussi pour gonfler l’autonomie de ses iPhone. En partie grâce à la puce A20 Pro, moins énergivore, les smartphones devraient jouir d’une autonomie de plus d’une journée, similaire à l’iPhone 17 Pro Max, en dépit d’une batterie plus petite. Apple précise que l’iPhone 18 Pro tient 24 heures en usage quotidien classique sur une seule charge, contre 30 heures pour la version Max, qui bénéficie d’une plus grosse batterie. C’est la « plus forte augmentation d’autonomie jamais réalisée sur iPhone ». Apple a également amélioré la charge rapide de ses nouveaux iPhone. Il suffit désormais de 15 minutes de charge pour récupérer 50% de batterie.
Prix et date de sortie des iPhone 18 Pro
Comme on le craignait, Apple a considérablement revu à la hausse le prix de l’iPhone Pro d’une année à l’autre. La marque californienne propose l’iPhone 18 Pro au prix de départ de 1 479 €. De son côté, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max est commercialisé au prix de départ de 1629 euros. Sans plus attendre, voici tous les prix en vigueur en France :
- iPhone 18 Pro 256 Go : 1 479 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 512 Go : 1 729 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 1 To : 2 229 €
- iPhone 18 Pro 2 To : 2 979 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 256 Go : 1 629 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 Go : 1 879 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 1 To : 2 379 €
- iPhone 18 Pro Max 2 To : 3 129 €
Fait inhabituel, Apple a décalé le calendrier de ses précommandes. Plutôt que d’ouvrir les précommandes le traditionnel vendredi suivant l’annonce, les précommandes ouvriront le samedi 12 septembre 2026. Ce changement permet d’éviter une ouverture des précommandes le 11 septembre, date du 25ᵉ anniversaire des attentats de 2001. Les nouveaux iPhone seront disponibles en magasin à partir du 18 septembre 2026. Allez-vous craquer pour cette nouvelle génération ? On attend votre avis dans les commentaires.

articles.title: Le Redmi Note 14 Pro+ défie les flagships de la concurrence avec -122€ pour les French Days
articles.text:
Le Redmi Note 14 Pro+ est l'un des smartphones les plus équilibrés du moment pour son prix, surtout que celui-ci passe de 471,99 euros à 349,99 euros sur Boulanger.
Avec la gamme Note 14, Xiaomi a complètement repensé ses smartphones et le modèle 14 Pro+ proposé ici en profite pleinement. C'est un smartphone milieu de gamme avec une base très solide, au design soigné et avec des performances en accord avec son placement. Si vous avez connu le Note 13 Pro+ il n'y a pas de vraie révolution, mais des évolutions discrètes et bienvenues. La baisse de prix dû aux French Days est un nouvel argument à mettre en sa faveur puisqu'il perd 122 euros sur Boulanger.
Voici le Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ à 349,99 € au lieu de 471,99 € sur Boulanger
Pourquoi choisir le Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ ?
- Parce que c'est un smartphone équilibré, à tous les niveaux, aussi bien la technique que la solidité, digne des flagships.
- Sa recharge ultra-rapide change la donne là où des grands noms plafonnent à 25 W, le Redmi Note 14 Pro+ monte à 120 W.
- Son écran premium pour tous les usages, une dalle AMOLED 1,5K lumineuse et bien calibrée idéale pour les loisirs.
Si l'offre présentée dans cet article n'est plus disponible, consultez la liste de prix ci-dessous pour trouver d'autres bons plans sur ce même produit. La mise à jour des prix est automatique.
Un smartphone bien calibré, mais sans révolution technique
Le Redmi Note 14 Pro+ séduit d'emblée par un design plus abouti que celui du Note 13 Pro+, avec notamment son îlot photo central qui lui donne des allures de smartphone premium. Pour l'écran, il est doté d'une dalle AMOLED 1,5L de 6,67 pouces pour une luminosité élevée et notre test à mis en avant une colorimétrie bien calibrée et un taux de rafraîchissement adaptatif 60/120 Hz. Tout ça pour garantir une belle lisibilité, même en plein soleil.
Les performances, en revanche, ne marquent pas de vrai saut générationnel par rapport au modèle précédent. On est en présence d'un Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 qui assure un usage fluide et une bonne tenue en jeu. Mais les gains sont vraiment modestes et certains basculements entre les applications peuvent accuser un petit délai, surtout sur la version 8 Go qui est celle proposée ici.
Photo, autonomie et logiciel : des atouts sérieux
On l'a évoqué au-dessus, petit retour sur la configuration photo du Redmi Note 14 Pro+ qui repose sur un capteur principal 200 Mpx honnête, capable de produire des clichés détaillés et bien contrastés avec une bonne luminosité. Par contre, l'ultra grand-angle 8 Mpx est à éviter, avec des images sombres, peu détaillées et une colorimétrie peu naturelle. Aussi, le zoom numérique au-delà de x4 montre ses limites avec un lissage trop présent et même quelques artefacts.
Par contre sur l'autonomie, on est sur un vrai point fort : une batterie de 5 110 mAh qui tient facilement une journée en utilisation classique, avec une charge 120 W HyperCharge qui permet de récupérer 100% en moins de 30 minutes. Il faut quand même nuancer l'enthousiasme avec l'absence de chargeur compatible, donc il faudra repasser à la caisse. Enfin, il faudra faire un peu de ménage à l'allumage pour le débarrasser d'une quinzaine de bloatwares agaçants.
✅ Les points forts
- Son design raffiné avec des finitions premium
- Un écran AMOLED 1,5K lumineux et bien calibré
- Une certification IP68 avec verre Gorilla Glass Victus 2
- Son autonomie confortable et la charge hyper rapide

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 9, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 9, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
From QNu Labs’ Rs 200-crore raise and leadership changes at Snap to payments moves by Jio Payment Solutions and Pluxee, YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Featured stories
QNu Labs raises Rs 200 crore in Series A1 round
Quantum cybersecurity startup QNu Labs raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest, with Sony Innovation Fund, Gaja Capital and Artha Ventures participating. The company will expand R&D and go-to-market in India and overseas.
Snap’s Ajit Mohan steps down as chief business officer
Ajit Mohan has stepped down as Snap’s Chief Business Officer and will return to Singapore to spend more time with his family. Snap has named EMEA President Ronan Harris as Chief Commercial Officer as part of the leadership changes.
Jacob Coxon warns labs of reckless superintelligence race
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has resigned after three years in pretraining roles across OpenAI and Anthropic, warning that top labs are racing toward self-improving superintelligence without adequate safety focus. He said the industry’s private misgivings about risks are greater than public statements suggest.
Jagriti helps women in eastern UP build digital businesses
Jagriti Sewa Sansthan’s Women’s Centre of Excellence in Deoria, Uttar Pradesh, is helping women build sustainable digital businesses through incubation, mentorship, market access and ecosystem building. The story traces Jagriti’s evolution from vocational training to enterprise support across Purvanchal.
IBM’s Rahul Rao on integrating AI into daily workflows
In an interview, IBM Distinguished Engineer Rahul Rao said AI delivers value only when employees can integrate it into everyday workflows, supported by governance, data and infrastructure readiness. He added that flexible architectures are needed to balance performance, energy efficiency, and cost across environments.
Funding news
Circolife raises $4.5M in pre-Series A round anchored by Jaisinghani
Cooling-as-a-service platform Circolife raised $4.5 million, Rs 40.45 crore, in a pre-Series A round anchored by Bharat Jaisinghani. Other participants included Nitish Mittersain, Intelliquity Ventures, Sumit Jalan, Siddharth and Anand Ladsariya, Anant Goenka, Sky Impact Capital, and the S N Damani and Vyom Wealth family offices. The company said proceeds will fund fleet expansion, national rollout, and its AI-augmented IoT platform.
Founded by Abhishek Murarka, Tushar Patil and Devanshu Mishra, Circolife offers subscription-based cooling for businesses. According to the company, it has about 10,000 active subscriptions across five cities and targets 40,000 units in 24 months. It added that connected sensors enable predictive maintenance, supported by in-house service teams and refurbishing facilities in Mumbai and Delhi.
Other news
Wipro and CrowdStrike launch CISO Command Center for enterprises
Wipro has launched a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) Command Center in collaboration with CrowdStrike to help enterprises shift from tool-driven security to a risk-led operating model. The centre uses Wipro Intelligence solutions, CyberTransform and CyberShield, with the CrowdStrike Falcon platform to unify endpoint, cloud, exposure and AI security with SOC-based detection and response.
Wipro said the centre will translate security signals into business risk intelligence. CrowdStrike’s Daniel Bernard said AI is changing both threats and defence. Wipro added it is a member of CrowdStrike’s Project QuiltWorks, a coalition focused on identifying, prioritising and remediating frontier AI risk.
Jio Payment Solutions launches cross-border payments for exporters
Jio Payment Solutions has launched cross-border payments after receiving RBI authorisation to operate as a payment aggregator for cross-border transactions. According to the company, exporters can accept international payments via virtual accounts, international cards, and local rails, with T+2 settlement and no rolling reserve, and receive eFIRA documentation within the same working day.
The company said its coverage spans around 50% of India’s export footprint and offers integrations from hosted checkouts and payment links to SDKs and APIs. Jio Payment Solutions has partnered with Citi as an Authorised Dealer Category-1 and for export collection accounts, and already operates as a payment aggregator for online and PoS transactions.
Multipl launches UPI spending app with liquid fund integration
Consumer fintech has Multipl launched a UPI-based spending account that keeps money for everyday expenses invested in eligible liquid mutual funds until payment. The company said a pilot with more than 20,000 users saw over Rs 20 crore invested and around Rs 4 crore in UPI transactions. It targets about 2 lakh users and Rs 200 crore in 12 months.
Multipl said it works with UTI, Axis, ICICI Prudential and HDFC mutual funds, and operates as a third party application provider on UPI. It will add bill payments on September 10. The Bengaluru firm says it has over 5 lakh users with investments facilitated exceeding Rs 150 crore.
ControlZ expands to 700 plus service centres across India
ControlZ has expanded its authorised service network to more than 700 centres, covering 31 states and union territories, 551 cities, and over 18,000 PIN codes. The company said the footprint is complemented by an 18-month warranty on renewed devices and a 24x7 AI-powered call centre.
According to the company, the expansion supports a broader ecosystem for premium renewed smartphones across renewal, distribution, warranty and after-sales service. ControlZ said it renews devices at component level and operates a Renew Hub that uses AI, automation and robotics.
FSID at IISc names Omprakash Subbarao as CEO
The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID) at IISc has adopted a new governance model and appointed Omprakash Subbarao as CEO, reporting to the FSID board. Prof Suryasarthy Bose will serve as professor-in-charge for institutional oversight. FSID said it aims to undertake 1,000 industry projects and build a portfolio of 300 deep-tech startups by 2030.
An IISc alumnus, Subbarao earlier led CORE Labs at FSID. The organisation said it will deepen corporate engagement and strengthen incubation via iHUB, where partners including BEML, Toyo Ink and Schaeffler have set up labs and workspaces.
Pluxee India receives RBI nod as payment aggregator
Pluxee India received RBI authorisation as a payment aggregator for both online and physical point-of-sale, complementing its existing prepaid payment instrument licence. The company said the approval enables merchant payment collection, settlement and refunds, and supports continued merchant acquiring under RBI’s licensing framework.
Pluxee said it supports more than 11,000 companies and 3.5 million consumers, with 150,000 plus meal merchant partners across over 2,200 cities. It operates on the RuPay network for additional benefits categories and has introduced AI-led bill processing, alongside the 2025 acquisition of corporate childcare benefits provider ProEves.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Crear música con IA basada en artistas reales no será un problema por este acuerdo de Suno con Warner Music y BMG
articles.text:
Suno formalizó un acuerdo con las discográficas Warner Music Group y BMG para lanzar una nueva generación de modelos de inteligencia artificial musical entrenados con catálogos licenciados.
El anuncio llega después de que la compañía enfrentara demandas por derechos de autor y es un giro hacia un esquema donde los artistas bajo contrato con esos sellos podrán participar de manera voluntaria en la creación de contenido generado por IA.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es el acuerdo de Suno para tener artistas reales
Suno presentó tres modelos: v6, v6-wild y v6-mini. El primero ofrece resultados pulidos para objetivos creativos definidos, mientras que v6-wild apunta a composiciones menos predecibles, orientadas a la exploración. Ambos quedaron reservados para los suscriptores de los planes Pro y Premier, que cuestan 8 y 24 dólares mensuales respectivamente en Estados Unidos.
El modelo v6-mini estará disponible de forma gratuita para todos los usuarios. La empresa anunció además que retirará sus sistemas anteriores para concentrar el servicio íntegramente en esta nueva generación, entrenada con datos distintos a los que motivaron las disputas legales previas.
PUBLICIDAD
El paquete incorpora herramientas dirigidas a productores: edición de fragmentos específicos de una canción mediante indicaciones o palabras de la letra, combinación de fuentes a través de mashups, aislamiento de elementos de audio y sampling. También permite generar instrucciones a partir de texto, audio, imágenes o video.
Suno lanzó su generación v6 en colaboración con Warner Music Group, BMG y Believe para ofrecer un modelo de música con IA basado en catálogos con licencia. El acuerdo permite a los artistas de esos sellos decidir si participan en experiencias generadas por inteligencia artificial y recibir una compensación cuando lo hagan.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo participarán los artistas bajo licencia
El mecanismo central del acuerdo es el consentimiento individual. Los artistas vinculados a Believe podrán elegir si se inscriben en las nuevas funciones de Suno, lo que introduce una lógica de adhesión voluntaria en un producto que hasta ahora operaba mediante generación automatizada sin distinción por titular de derechos.
“Lo que viene a continuación es un nuevo tipo de producto que estamos desarrollando: experiencias opcionales creadas en torno a artistas concretos, en las que los artistas pueden elegir participar y recibir una remuneración cuando lo hagan”, afirmó el presidente ejecutivo de Suno, Mikey Shulman, cofundador de la empresa en 2022.
PUBLICIDAD
Believe, además, abre una vía de distribución: las canciones generadas en la plataforma podrían llegar a tiendas digitales y servicios de streaming a través de esa discográfica y de TuneCore, según reportó The Next Web. Esto conectaría producciones hechas con IA con los canales que usan los lanzamientos musicales convencionales.
Suno no detalló todavía tarifas, criterios de reparto ni mecanismos concretos para calcular los ingresos que recibirían los artistas participantes. El director de productos de la compañía, Jack Brody, explicó que el objetivo es ampliar las fuentes de ingreso para todos los involucrados: “Una gran parte de este lanzamiento es crear flujos de ingresos adicionales”, señaló en una entrevista.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa también modificó las condiciones de uso general. Las canciones creadas en el nivel gratuito pueden reproducirse y compartirse, pero ya no descargarse. Los usuarios de pago tienen límites mensuales de descarga y pueden adquirir descargas adicionales al alcanzar el tope, una medida que se suma a las marcas de agua y huellas digitales que Suno comenzó a incorporar el mes pasado.
Un acuerdo después de conflictos entre la IA y las disqueras
El calendario del lanzamiento está ligado a un pacto previo. Suno resolvió en noviembre de 2025 una demanda por derechos de autor presentada por Warner Music Group, que la acusaba de haber utilizado música protegida para entrenar sus modelos sin autorización. Entre los compromisos de ese acuerdo figuraba el desarrollo de sistemas licenciados más avanzados y el retiro de los modelos cuestionados.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía enfrenta, sin embargo, frentes judiciales que el nuevo acuerdo no resuelve. En Alemania, un tribunal determinó en 2026 que Suno infringió derechos de autor en un caso presentado por la sociedad de gestión colectiva GEMA. Universal Music Group, además, no figura entre los socios de este lanzamiento.
El caso de Udio, competidor directo de Suno, ilustra la falta de consenso en la industria. Udio llegó a un acuerdo con Universal Music Group y Warner Music Group el año pasado, pero Sony continúa demandando a esa plataforma por el supuesto uso de más de 30.000 grabaciones, con un reclamo de hasta 4.500 millones de dólares en daños.
PUBLICIDAD
Suno recaudó recientemente más de 400 millones de dólares en una ronda de financiación que valoró a la empresa en 5.400 millones de dólares, y acumula más de 819 millones de dólares en financiamiento total según datos de PitchBook.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12 y Ultra 4: el gran salto está en salud, pero ahora también pueden recordar lo que hemos hablado
articles.text:
Hay una enorme diferencia entre saber cuántas veces ha latido nuestro corazón y entender qué nos está diciendo ese dato. El Apple Watch lleva años acumulando información sobre nuestra actividad, sueño y salud, pero esta generación intenta reducir precisamente esa distancia entre medir e interpretar. Los nuevos Series 12 y Ultra 4 parten de una renovación profunda de sus sensores y de un chip preparado para trabajar con mucha más información durante todo el día. Y ahora el reloj también empieza a prestar atención a otra fuente de información que siempre hemos tenido alrededor al más puro estilo Plaud: nuestras conversaciones.
Apple ha presentado ambos modelos durante "Un rayo de wow.", la misma keynote que ha servido para enseñar los iPhone 18 Pro y 18 Pro Max y su primer teléfono plegable. El Series 12 continúa como el reloj pensado para un público más amplio, mientras que el Ultra 4 conserva su orientación hacia deporte, aventura y actividades prolongadas. Buena parte de la tecnología que los hace avanzar es compartida: Health Sensing System, chip S11 y una nueva capa de software que intenta convertir las señales recogidas durante el día en información que resulte más fácil utilizar.
Más datos, pero también más contexto
El nuevo sistema incorpora sensores cardiacos ópticos y eléctricos y unos LED verdes más grandes y eficientes. Gracias a ellos, el reloj mide la frecuencia cardiaca cada cinco segundos de forma pasiva durante todo el día y registra la variabilidad cardiaca hasta 24 veces más frecuentemente. Todo ello alimenta readiness, que cruza actividad reciente, carga de entrenamiento, constantes y puntuación de sueño para ofrecernos un valor entre 0 y 10 acompañado de una recomendación sobre cómo afrontar la jornada. No es una fotografía fija: el resultado puede actualizarse si nuestro estado o actividad cambian.
En el Series 12, Apple acompaña esa renovación interna con algunos cambios tangibles. Sigue disponible en 42 y 46 mm y recupera la caja de cerámica, desaparecida desde el Series 5, ahora en blanco perla y azul noche. Los modelos de aluminio incorporan Ceramic Shield 2, un material que la compañía cifra como un 60% más resistente que el Ion-X de la generación anterior. Sus 24 horas de autonomía cotidiana no cambian, pero los entrenamientos al aire libre alcanzan 10 horas y 15 minutos conectado permiten obtener hasta otras 12 horas de batería.
En el Ultra 4, la batería se convierte en una diferencia mucho más seria. El reloj alcanza ahora hasta 50 horas de uso normal y 84 horas en bajo consumo, además de sumar hasta 18 horas con una carga de 15 minutos. Para quienes realmente lo utilicen en actividades largas, Extended Workout ofrece hasta 25 horas manteniendo GPS y frecuencia cardiaca, mientras que Max Extended Workout eleva el registro hasta 45 horas con posiciones GPS cada segundo. La compañía mantiene así el planteamiento del Ultra como el reloj destinado a quienes necesitan llevar estas capacidades bastante más lejos.
El S11 abre además un camino que poco tiene que ver con contar pasos. Audio Intelligence utiliza el micrófono del reloj para reconocer sonidos y trabajar con nuestras conversaciones: con Siri Recap activado, Apple Watch puede generar automáticamente un título y varios puntos clave cuando terminamos de hablar, mientras que Live Rewind recupera como texto los 15 segundos anteriores para consultar algo que acabamos de perder.
Somos nosotros quienes decidimos cuándo utiliza estas funciones y Apple afirma que el sistema no almacena grabaciones, porque el audio bruto se procesa en un entorno aislado del chip y se elimina inmediatamente. Se trata de una solución interesante, aunque probablemente también despertará preguntas acerca de privacidad. Siri Recap y Live Rewind llegarán en beta más adelante y, alto muy importante, no estarán disponibles inicialmente en la Unión Europea.
Precio y disponibilidad
Apple ha abierto las reservas de ambos relojes y su llegada a tiendas está prevista para el 18 de septiembre. El Apple Watch Series 12 cuesta desde 449 euros en España, mientras que el Apple Watch Ultra 4 parte de 899 euros.

articles.title: O que é Hi-Res Audio? Saiba como aproveitar o padrão de qualidade sonora • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
O que é Hi-Res Audio? Saiba como aproveitar o padrão de qualidade sonora
O áudio Hi-Res promove um som mais fiel às gravações originais, sem perdas de qualidade por compressão, como ocorre com CDs e MP3
O Hi-Res Audio eleva a experiência sonora ao capturar o som com profundidade de bits e taxa de amostragem superiores, preservando a fidelidade original da gravação. Com isso, a qualidade de áudio entrega uma riqueza de detalhes, texturas e um palco sonoro mais amplo.
O formato está disponível em plataformas de streaming como Apple Music e Tidal, além de arquivos digitais FLAC e mídias físicas dedicadas. Contudo, para aproveitar o som com alta fidelidade, é recomendável utilizar fones de ouvido ou caixas com conexão via cabo.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te explica o que é áudio Hi-Res, suas principais características e vantagens.
O que é Hi-Res Audio?
O Hi-Res Audio (High-Resolution Audio) é um formato de áudio digital que oferece qualidade superior à do CD ou de formatos comprimidos (MP3) ao capturar o som com mais fidelidade. Isso é possível devido a uma taxa de amostragem (sampling rate) e uma profundidade de bits (bit depth) mais altas.
Quais as características do áudio Hi-Res?
O áudio Hi-Res entrega uma experiência sonora mais refinada ao preservar cada detalhe da gravação original, sem os cortes da compressão comum. Suas principais características incluem:
- Profundidade de bits elevada (24-bit): registra o volume com precisão extrema, criando uma gradação de mais de 16 milhões de níveis sonoros e eliminando ruídos indesejados em trechos sutis;
- Taxa de amostragem superior (48 a 192 kHz): captura a onda sonora até 192 mil vezes por segundo, garantindo frequências agudas mais limpas e sem distorções digitais;
- Amplo alcance dinâmico: a diferença entre o som mais baixo e o mais alto fica mais clara, permitindo ouvir instrumentações e detalhes sutis com altíssima definição;
- Codificação sem perdas (Lossless): preserva 100% dos dados originais da gravação por meio de formatos como FLAC e WAV, sem descartar frequências para diminuir o arquivo;
- Arquivos e consumo maiores: a alta densidade de dados gera arquivos mais pesados, exigindo mais espaço de armazenamento e uma internet mais veloz para streaming;
- Necessidade de hardware dedicado: exige equipamentos compatíveis, como fones de alta qualidade e um conversor digital para analógico (DAC), para revelar todo o potencial do som.
Onde o Hi-Res Audio está disponível?
Os ouvintes podem curtir o Hi-Res Audio por meio de mídias digitais, plataformas de streaming e formatos físicos dedicados. A disponibilidade varia de acordo com o serviço ou o suporte do dispositivo:
- Plataformas de streaming e download: serviços como Apple Music, Tidal e Amazon Music Unlimited entregam músicas via streaming ou downloads nos formatos FLAC e ALAC sem custo adicional na assinatura básica.
- Formatos de arquivos digitais: arquivos em FLAC, WAV e ALAC mantêm a qualidade de áudio de estúdio e podem ser armazenados e reproduzidos localmente em computadores, celulares e tocadores portáteis;
- Mídias físicas dedicadas: mídias de alta capacidade, como o Blu-Ray Audio e o DVD-Audio, utilizam codificações puras, como PCM e DSD, para entregar faixas de alta definição sem depender da internet.
Posso ouvir Hi-Res no Spotify, Apple Music ou Deezer?
A disponibilidade de Hi-Res Audio varia entre os serviços de streaming e de compra de músicas digitais. Enquanto algumas plataformas oferecem suporte completo a arquivos de alta resolução, outras se limitam à qualidade de CD ou transmissão comprimida com perdas de dados.
| Serviço | Suporte a Hi-Res Audio | Qualidade Máxima de Som | Formato Utilizado | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Spotify | Não (Apenas Lossless/CD) | 24-bit / 44.1 kHz | FLAC / Ogg Vorbis | 
| Apple Music | Sim | Até 24-bit / 192 kHz | ALAC (Apple Lossless) | 
| Deezer | Não (Apenas Lossless/CD) | 16-bit / 44.1 kHz | FLAC | 
| Tidal | Sim | Até 24-bit / 192 kHz | FLAC | 
| Qobuz | Sim | Até 24-bit / 192 kHz | FLAC | 
| Amazon Music Unlimited | Sim | Até 24-bit / 192 kHz | FLAC/PCM | 
| Bandcamp | Sim (Depende do artista) | Até 24-bit / 96 kHz+ | FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF | 
Posso ouvir Hi-Res em qualquer fone de ouvido?
Você pode reproduzir arquivos Hi-Res em qualquer fone, mas só aproveitará a qualidade de áudio máxima ao usar modelos cabeados conectados a um conversor digital-analógico (DAC). Esse equipamento é essencial para processar e entregar taxas altíssimas de até 24 bits e 192 kHz sem nenhuma perda de dados.
Fones Bluetooth têm limitações porque a tecnologia de transmissão de áudio sem fio comprime o sinal por meio de codecs como AAC e SBC. Embora opções avançadas como LDAC cheguem perto do nível Hi-Res, restrições do próprio ecossistema do dispositivo ainda impedem uma transmissão de som “100% pura”.
O áudio Hi-Res é o mesmo que o áudio Lossless?
Não, o áudio Lossless garante que nenhum dado sonoro seja descartado durante a compressão de um arquivo. Ele preserva a fidelidade exata da gravação, mas limita-se tradicionalmente à qualidade técnica padrão encontrada nos CDs convencionais (16-bit e 44.1 kHz).
A diferença é que o Hi-Res Audio se refere às faixas de alta resolução que ultrapassam as especificações do CD, exigindo 24-bit e taxas acima de 48 kHz. Embora um arquivo Hi-Res normalmente também seja lossless, seu foco é capturar mais detalhes e nuances da música.
Hi-Res e Hi-Fi são a mesma coisa?
Não, o Hi-Fi (High Fidelity) é um conceito amplo que define a capacidade de um sistema de reproduzir o som com o máximo de fidelidade e o mínimo de distorção. É um padrão de desempenho para equipamentos, independentemente da especificação técnica do arquivo.
O Hi-Res é uma categoria técnica específica de áudio digital, que exige arquivos gravados em 24-bit e taxas a partir de 48 kHz. Enquanto o Hi-Fi se refere à qualidade geral do equipamento de reprodução, o Hi-Res define a resolução exata e certificada do arquivo transmitido.
Então, qual a vantagem de ouvir músicas em alta resolução?
O áudio em alta resolução oferece uma experiência sonora muito mais rica e fiel ao estúdio, aproximando o ouvinte da intenção original dos artistas. Ao preservar a integridade total do som, o formato traz vantagens claras para quem busca máxima qualidade:
- Riqueza de detalhes e texturas: a alta taxa de amostragem captura mais dados por segundo, revelando sutilezas como a reverberação do ambiente, o toque nas cordas e a respiração dos artistas;
- Agudos limpos e sem distorções: frequências elevadas eliminam ranhuras e artefatos digitais, garantindo um som mais suave e livre da aspereza comum em arquivos comprimidos;
- Palco sonoro mais amplo: a precisão do áudio melhora a percepção de instrumentos, criando uma sensação espacial tridimensional em que cada elemento ocupa seu próprio lugar;
- Fidelidade à masterização original: garante que você ouça a faixa exatamente como ela foi gravada e produzida pelos engenheiros de som, sem cortes de frequência ou perda de dinâmica.

articles.title: Corsair made a $200 gaming chair and then tested it like it was going into battle
articles.text:
Gaming Comfort: Gaming chairs are often one of the most overlooked pieces of furniture in a gaming setup. While luxury "thrones" can be left to customers with truly deep pockets, most gamers should at least consider investing in a somewhat expensive chair to ease the discomfort that comes with long gaming sessions.
Corsair recently launched the TC80 Gaming Chair, a new armchair designed to provide a durable and comfortable seating option for PC-focused gaming setups. The Fremont-based corporation highlights how its new chair has undergone more than 30 durability and safety tests, suggesting that it should accommodate gamers with a wide range of body types.
The TC80 Gaming Chair meets the BIFMA X5.1 and EN 1335 standards for office chairs, Corsair said. The chair underwent a series of demanding durability, stability, and weight-load tests, with Corsair particularly proud of how its new product survived the onslaught.
These tests included dropping a 136kg load onto the center of the seat, applying a 1,001N load to the backrest for 60 seconds, and placing 13 heavy discs against the backrest. Furthermore, the chair survived 100,000 cycles of a 57kg weight falling onto the seat, 60,000 cycles of 400N being applied to each armrest, and 120,000 swivel-test cycles with 122kg placed on the seat at both its maximum and minimum height.
The TC80 Gaming Chair provides a "generously" wide and flat seat with plush padding, breathable fabric upholstery, and 100mm of adjustable seat height. There is even a detachable neck pillow for people who like to alternate between office work sessions and more relaxing activities. The chair's stability comes from a steel five-star base, 50mm casters, and a Class 4 steel gas lift that should last for years.
Talking about comfort, Corsair's new chair offers a recline range of 90° to 115°. Users can adjust and lock the chair at their preferred angle, so there is no need to settle for a fixed position straight out of the box.
Corsair is already selling the TC80 Gaming Chair through its own store and other major retailers. The chair costs $200 in the US, while customers in Europe and the UK can get it for €180 and £170, respectively. The company's official announcement provides a full list of regional launch prices.
Corsair also highlights the TC80 as an entry-level product in its growing lineup of gaming chairs. The company already offers more expensive models, such as the TC100 Relaxed and the premium TC500 Luxe.
The TC500 comes with a €550 price tag in Europe, which is still a relatively affordable purchase compared with some truly expensive chairs, such as the obscenely priced Herman Miller x Logitech Embody. For now, I think I'll stick with my cheap Songmics gaming chair.

articles.title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
articles.text:
Apple announced the Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 today. Both include a new “Health Sensing System” and S11 chip that give the devices the “most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable,” Apple claimed during its fall event.
Both watches will use the new S11 chip alongside the new “Health Sensing System,” allowing the watches to deliver higher-frequency heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV) measurements than prior Apple Watches.
The Health Sensing System includes redesigned photodiodes organized in a ring to capture light more efficiently and a larger electrode surface area for better skin contact. Additionally, the green LEDs on each Watch’s optical heart sensor are supposed to be bigger and more power-efficient and measure the user’s heart rate every five seconds. Users will be able to view their heart rate in real time with a new heart rate watch face special feature (also known as a complication).
The new watches can take HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequently than their predecessors, Apple said. HRV is an indicator of how well the body is able to adapt to changes such as stress and exercise.
“Overnight vitals now includes recovery HRV measurements analyzed against a user’s personal baseline, providing a more complete view of their health status. A new daytime vitals view lets users toggle between overnight and daytime metrics, and can potentially spot shifts in their metrics before they show up overnight,” Apple said in a press release.

articles.title: Apple unveils Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
articles.text:
Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 at its Sept. 9 event, with a big focus on Apple Intelligence and health and fitness.
One of the big new features is the Health Sensing System, which includes upgraded hardware to better track health metrics. That includes more electrodes, bigger photodiodes for better light capture, and larger, brighter green LEDs.
Apple says the new system can check heart rate 60x more frequently than before and can sample heart rate variability (HRV) every 5 minutes for the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable when compared against competitors using an ECG as a reference.
Another new feature is Health Age, which uses various metrics like sleep and biomarkers from blood to show what your overall health is like.
A big part of that is a new Health app coming later this year, which includes an all-new design and several of the new features.
Another watch-related announcement was Audio Intelligence, which aims to make sense of what you hear. There’s Live Rewind, which lets you press the digital crown on the Apple Watch to view a transcript of recent speech.
Sound Recognition is now on the Apple Watch as well, which allows the watch to listen for certain sounds and alert people to them. These include sirens, alarms, doorbells, or the sound of a baby crying. Apple Watch uses on-device intelligence to detect and notify users of those sounds.
Siri Recap is another Audio Intelligence feature that can create summaries of conversations for later review. Apple was quick to note that this all happens on device and thus shouldn’t be a privacy concern.
Apple Watch Series 12
Apple touts the Watch Series 12 as being as “individual as the person wearing it,” offering the wearable in a variety of colours and finishes. That includes dark bronze, black, light gold, and space grey aluminum, as well as radiant gold and natural titanium. Plus, there’s a new ceramic option in both white and blue shades.
Watch Series 12 sports Ceramic Shield 2 glass on the face, making it more durable than before.
Apple Watch Ultra 4
Meanwhile, Watch Ultra 4 remains the ultimate sports and adventure smartwatch, boasting two-day battery life. Specifically, Apple boasts up to 50 hours of battery on the Ultra 4, extendable to 84 hours in Low Power Mode.
Elsewhere, Apple says it redesigned the pedometer model for more accurate step tracking, distance measurements, and more.
In Canada, the Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $549, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $1,099.

articles.title: Apple’s new CEO is reviving a Steve Jobs strategy from 25 years ago | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple CEO John Ternus wants you to know that the iPhone isn’t going anywhere.
Ternus threw his weight behind the venerable device on Wednesday during his first keynote as CEO, placing it firmly at the center of Apple’s product strategy for the AI era.
“There’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” he said.
This contrasts with the approach taken by former CEO Tim Cook, who tried time and again to convince Wall Street that Apple was more than just the iPhone.
Ternus’ pitch is also a rebuttal to pundits who have recently cast doubt on the iPhone. “The smartphone’s days are numbered,” said one headline. “The Tim Cook era is coming to a close with an existential challenge for Apple: figuring out what comes after the iPhone,” said another article.
But it’s not just about the hardware. Ternus has put the iPhone at the center of his “intelligent personal assistant” strategy, a vision that could define the company for years to come. Steve Jobs did something similar in 2001 with the Mac, less than 10 months before he announced the iPod.
At the time, many observers thought the PC’s days were numbered. At a Macworld New York keynote, Jobs called out bearish quotes from industry wonks like Walt Mossberg and the leaders of Compaq and Gateway.
“This is what everyone else is telling us. That our PC is waning if not the hole being dug,” Jobs said at the time, pointing at a tombstone for the “Beloved PC” on the screen behind him. “We don’t think the PC is dying at all. We don’t think the PC is moving away from the center at all. We think it’s evolving, just like it has since it was invented.”
“We think the PC is on the threshold of entering its third great age,” Jobs added, a prediction driven by the proliferation of digital devices at the time, including camcorders, digital cameras, and DVD players.
The Mac would form the center of a “digital hub” that would connect these disparate devices and, in Jobs’ words, “add value” to all of them.
Later that year, Jobs pulled the iPod out of his pocket, a device seemingly developed to answer the question, “Why do you still need a PC?” The device turned out to be an enormous hit, driving Apple’s profits quarter after quarter and ultimately helping lead to the development of the iPhone.
Today, with the iPhone on the cusp of its 20th anniversary, Ternus is facing a version of the same question Jobs took on in 2001. We don’t know if Ternus is quietly sitting on an iPod-like product, one that will secure the iPhone’s position a Apple’s hub for years to come. But he is firmly rebutting the idea that the iPhone is past its prime.
“If you were designing the ideal version of this hub from scratch, how would you do it?” Ternus asked, before listing the ingredients: a powerful processor, high-resolution cameras, persistent networking, and on-device AI.
It helps that the iPhone is one of the most powerful personal computing devices around, giving it an edge in the compute-hungry AI era. Its portability and adaptability make it, for many people, the only computing device they need. Even among those who own laptops and iPads, the iPhone is often the one device they can’t live without. Plenty of people leave home without their laptops. Almost no one leaves without their phones.
That combination of power and portability has given Apple a privileged position in the AI world. Other companies have attempted to unseat the iPhone with all manner of wearable devices, but none have succeeded.
Instead of sidelining the iPhone in favor of the next flashy thing, Ternus is leaning into it instead. In a way, he’s bringing Apple around to what the rest of us already know: The iPhone is pretty great, and maybe we don’t need to replace it with something else. Yet.

articles.title: Google obéit à l'Europe et annonce une mauvaise nouvelle aux utilisateurs de son moteur de recherche
articles.text:
Entre Google et la Commission européenne, le bras de fer dure depuis plus de quinze ans, à coups d’amendes milliardaires et de recours interminables. Le dernier épisode se joue depuis le 23 juillet, date à laquelle Bruxelles a infligé 460 millions d’euros au géant pour avoir favorisé ses services d’achat, d’hôtellerie, de transport et de sport dans les résultats. Google déploie désormais sa réponse dans tout l’Espace économique européen, en prévenant qu’elle constituera la plus forte baisse de qualité de ses 29 ans d’histoire.
Comparateurs en tête de gondole, services maison rétrogradés
Concrètement, les pages de résultats européennes accueillent deux nouveaux modules. Le premier met en avant les comparateurs, agences de voyage en ligne et autres métamoteurs sur les recherches d’hôtels, de vols, de trains et cars longue distance ou de produits, le service le mieux classé s’affichant déployé par défaut, photos et tarifs compris. Le second réserve un espace aux entreprises en direct (hôteliers, compagnies, boutiques), que Google alimentera en aspirant leurs données publiques, sans intégration technique à prévoir. Les requêtes locales, restaurants et adresses de proximité en tête, suivront plus tard.
Lire aussi : Google Search, c’est terminé : 5 moteurs de recherche européens pour le remplacer
Dans le même mouvement, le carrousel maison qui trustait le haut de page recule nettement plus bas, et certaines informations pratiques disparaissent, à commencer par les prix affichés en temps réel. « Ces changements dégradent l’expérience des Européens : ils renforcent les intermédiaires en ligne au détriment des entreprises locales et suppriment des fonctionnalités utiles au quotidien », attaque Nick Fox, vice-président de Google chargé de la recherche. Le règlement sur les marchés numériques interdit pourtant une chose assez simple : réserver un traitement de faveur à ses propres services. Google disposait de 60 jours pour se conformer, un délai qui court jusqu’à la fin du mois. Un air de déjà-vu, d’ailleurs, puisque l’affaire Google Shopping s’était soldée dès 2017 par 2,4 milliards d’euros d’amende pour un grief voisin.
Réserver un vol ou un hôtel ne se passera plus comme avant
Pour vous, le changement se verra dès la prochaine recherche de week-end. Taper « hôtel Lisbonne » fera remonter les plateformes spécialisées en haut de page, tandis que la carte et les tarifs en direct auxquels Google vous avait habitué se feront plus discrets, voire absents. Il faudra donc rouvrir plusieurs onglets et comparer soi-même, comme au bon vieux temps des années 2010 (le clic supplémentaire, cette madeleine). L’algorithme de Google continue par ailleurs de décider quels services remontent : la mécanique du classement, elle, reste entre les mains de la maison.
Reste l’addition, et elle promet d’être salée pour les professionnels du tourisme. Selon Google, les précédentes mesures de conformité au DMA ont déjà coûté aux entreprises européennes 30 % de leur trafic gratuit de réservation directe, et le groupe projette un impact du même ordre pour cette nouvelle salve. Les comparateurs décrochent la visibilité qu’ils réclamaient depuis des années ; les hôteliers et compagnies devront espérer que le module qui leur est réservé compense la vitrine perdue. Quant à Bruxelles, elle n’a pas encore dit si cette copie suffisait à clore le dossier.
